newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees exports still spurring economy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees exports still spurring economy.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Tuesday that exports would continue to be one of the main motors of economic growth in 1997, though he also saw an important role for domestic demand.
Citing a Banco de Mexico survey of top Mexican exporters, he said he was confident exports would not taper off.

"The 100 largest exporting companies in this country are increasing their investments by 50 percent, expanding productive capacity," Ortiz said during a question and answer session in the Mexican Congress.
Contributing to growth has been an increase in public sector investment, Ortiz said, which grew around 11 percent in real terms in the first half of 1996.

He also said that there was a small increase in public sector consumption and he said there was evidence of slight improvement in domestic demand through retail and wholesale sales statistics and car sales.
Ortiz defended the government's record in providing funding to some of Mexico's poorest states, where there has been increasing social unrest and guerrilla violence since last year's economic crisis.
He said the federal contribution to Mexican states' budgets will grow five percent in real terms in 1996, though it fell due to seasonal factors about 1.5 percent in the first six months of the year.
